privacy.description: Privacy policy for mirroview, including local video sharing, permissions, diagnostics, and support email.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.lede: This policy describes the current mirroview iPhone and iPad release and this website.
privacy.section1.heading: Who to contact
privacy.section1.p1: mirroview is an independent iPhone and iPad app. For privacy questions, email {email}.
privacy.section2.heading: What the app does
privacy.section2.p1: The app supports local screen sharing between two iPhones or iPads running iOS or iPadOS 17 or newer. It uses authenticated local discovery and signaling. A reachable shared Wi-Fi network uses WebRTC video. An authenticated nearby video route is also available when device and system conditions permit. Connection quality, system support, and wireless conditions determine availability. Both people must confirm each session. The sender must also authorize screen capture through the iOS or iPadOS system interface. The app does not transmit audio.
privacy.section2.p2: Live video is sent to the connected viewer. We do not run an account service or an operator video server for the current release, and the app does not upload session video to us. A viewer can still save or externally photograph what appears on their device.
privacy.section3.heading: Permissions and local data
privacy.section3.list1.item1: Local Network: Finds and connects to the other device on your local network.
privacy.section3.list1.item2: Camera: Scans an invitation QR code when you choose to scan. Watching a screen does not require camera access.
privacy.section3.list1.item3: Screen capture: iOS or iPadOS asks the sender to authorize an entire-screen share. The app cannot silently grant this permission. The sender can then open other apps, including Camera, to show their screens.
privacy.section3.list1.item4: Device orientation: The app uses captured-frame orientation metadata to display shared content.
privacy.section3.p2: Short-lived invitations and connection data are used for a session. Depending on the iOS or iPadOS version (17 or later), the app may temporarily place an invitation and status files in a shared app container so its screen broadcast extension can start. The extension consumes the invitation file. The app does not use these files as a video archive.
privacy.section4.heading: Storage and diagnostics
privacy.section4.p1: The app does not create an account or save session photos and videos. It keeps bounded diagnostic events on the device, including app and iOS or iPadOS versions, device model, connection stages, numeric errors, and media counters. The records exclude invitation QR codes, keys, IP addresses, Wi-Fi names, full SDP/ICE, and media. A random identifier is used for each process launch; it is not a persistent device identifier. Logs rotate locally. You may export a ZIP through the system share sheet, and only the latest three exports are retained in the app cache. The app does not automatically upload diagnostics. Send an export to support only if you want us to review it. Deleting the app removes its local diagnostic files; files you exported elsewhere remain under your control.
privacy.section5.heading: Website and email
privacy.section5.p1: We do not add analytics, advertising, tracking pixels, or contact forms to these pages. Hosting and network providers may add security checks and process ordinary access data needed to serve and protect the pages. If you email us, you choose what to include. We and our email provider process your address and message to answer you and keep support correspondence. To ask about or request deletion of an email you sent, contact the same address.
privacy.section6.heading: Changes
privacy.section6.p1: We may update this policy when the app or site changes. The date above identifies the latest version.
privacy.title: Privacy policy | mirroview
support.description: Get help with mirroview local screen sharing, pairing, permissions, and video connection issues.
support.heading: Support
support.lede: Get help with pairing, permissions, and a missing video picture.
support.notice: Email {email} for support or privacy questions.
support.section1.heading: Start a session
support.section1.list1.item1: Use two iPhones or iPads running iOS or iPadOS 17 or newer. For your first session, connect both devices to the same reachable local Wi-Fi network. The app also includes nearby sharing, whose availability depends on the devices, system support, and wireless conditions. Keep Wi-Fi enabled on both devices. Internet access is not required for the video session.
support.section1.list1.item2: On the sending device, choose to share. The main share button starts an entire-screen session.
support.section1.list1.item3: On the viewing device, choose to watch and scan the invitation QR code. If scanning is unavailable, use the paste-invitation option on the home screen to paste an invitation copied from the sending device.
support.section1.list1.item4: Check the invitation and confirm on both devices. The sender must also approve the iOS or iPadOS screen capture prompt.
support.section1.p2: After screen sharing starts, the sender can open Camera or another app. The viewer sees the screen, subject to iOS or iPadOS capture restrictions.
support.section2.heading: Export diagnostics
support.section2.p1: On the home screen, tap the version number six times, choose Export logs ZIP, and use the system share sheet. Export from both devices after a failure. Include the approximate time and whether each device was connected to a router. Do not post diagnostic files publicly.
support.section3.heading: If the devices cannot connect
support.section3.list1.item1: Try connecting both devices to the same reachable local Wi-Fi and confirming that the network allows devices to communicate with each other. Guest or isolated networks may block this.
support.section3.list1.item2: Allow Local Network access for mirroview in iOS or iPadOS Settings.
support.section3.list1.item3: Start a fresh session and scan or paste the new invitation. Old invitations expire.
support.section3.list1.item4: Keep both apps open during pairing and try again if the network changes.
support.section4.heading: If the viewer sees no picture
support.section4.list1.item1: Confirm the session on both devices and approve the iOS or iPadOS screen share prompt on the sending device.
support.section4.list1.item2: Check that the sender has not paused or stopped sharing.
support.section4.list1.item3: Try showing an ordinary app screen. Some protected content cannot be captured.
support.section4.list1.item4: End the session and start a new one if the connection drops.
support.section4.p2: Audio is not part of the current app. A viewer may still capture a copy of visible video through their device.
support.section5.heading: Write to us
support.section5.p1: Include the app version, both iPhone or iPad models, iOS or iPadOS versions, what you were trying to share, and the steps that led to the problem. Tell us whether pairing failed or video was blank after both people confirmed. Do not email invitation QR codes, passwords, private screen images, or diagnostic archives unless you intend to share them.

terms.description: mirroview terms of use and limits for local screen sharing on iPhone and iPad.
terms.heading: Terms of use
terms.lede: These terms cover use of the mirroview app and this website.
terms.section1.heading: Sharing and responsibility
terms.section1.p1: Use mirroview only when you have the right to share the content and both people agree to the session. The sender starts screen sharing and authorizes screen capture through the iOS or iPadOS system interface. Either person can end a session.
terms.section1.p2: Before sharing your screen, check for notifications, messages, personal information, and anything else you do not want the viewer to see. The viewer may take screenshots, record their screen, or photograph the display. Do not assume content becomes private again after it has been shown.
terms.section2.heading: Connection and content limits
terms.section2.p1: Both iPhones or iPads must run iOS or iPadOS 17 or newer. For your first connection, use the same reachable local Wi-Fi network and keep Wi-Fi enabled on both devices. The app also includes an authenticated nearby screen-sharing route, but it does not guarantee video connectivity in every router-free or mixed-network setup. Internet access is not required for a local video session. Discovery or pairing alone does not guarantee a video connection. Performance and availability vary with device, system version, wireless conditions, and system permissions. Some protected content may be hidden or blocked by iOS, iPadOS, or the source app. mirroview does not transmit audio.
terms.section3.heading: Availability and updates
terms.section3.p1: Updates may be required. If you use a prerelease or beta version of mirroview, its features may change, pause, or stop working. Do not rely on the app for safety-critical monitoring, emergency communication, or preserving evidence.
terms.section4.heading: Acceptable use
terms.section4.p1: Do not use the app to share content without required consent, violate another person's privacy or rights, or break applicable law. You are responsible for what you choose to show and for any content you save as a viewer.
terms.section5.heading: Disclaimers and rights
terms.section5.p1: We provide the app and site as available. We do not promise uninterrupted service, a particular frame rate, or compatibility with every device, network, or protected app. To the extent permitted by applicable law, we are not responsible for losses caused by network failure, interrupted capture, or a viewer's actions. These terms do not exclude or limit rights or remedies that applicable law does not allow us to exclude or limit.
terms.section6.heading: Changes and contact
terms.section6.p1: We may update these terms. Continued use after an update means you accept the updated terms where the law permits. If you have a question, email {email}.
